factual_methodology.summary: Original Treasury August TIC release and instrument table, ICI October long-term/ETF/MMF data, BEA Q2 international investment statistics, World Gold Council September 2026 gold ETF series, BlackRock Q3 release and IMF October 2026 GFSR independently checked against numerical claims, timing and reporting populations; flow/stock/valuation/control separated.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Direct bilingual evidence-driven opening, consistent financial definitions, non-duplicated original/secondary investment data and plausible alternative transmission channels; no public QA labels or recommendations.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Three matched numeric charts, two extended evidentiary tables and an origin-destination matrix, one flow and one map in each locale; matching numeric series and physically meaningful units.

research_depth.summary: More than 2200 substantive words in each language; portfolio instrument composition, valuation, geographic attribution, fund wrappers, institutional liquidity, physical gold and three falsifiable paths.

evidence_traceability.summary: At least four distinct primary-source hosts with citations for TIC, ICI, BEA, WGC, IMF and BlackRock; different observation windows explicitly separated.

counterfactual_review.summary: Persistence, sovereign yield/collateral tightening and geographic productive reallocation scenarios each specify independent testable outcomes.

contrary_evidence: July TIC adjusted securities flow negative even though August recovered; one month cannot prove persistence.
Treasury bills and bank dollar liabilities contracted despite August securities inflows.
Domestic-equity redemptions coexist with positive domestic-equity ETF issuance; a wrapper change cannot be attributed to identical investors.
BEA Q2 external asset/liability changes mainly include market valuation, unlike TIC transacted flows.
Gold ETF physical tonnage rose despite falling assets under management.
limitations: August Treasury portfolio data are not an October 19 market close; latest long-term ICI is the week ending 7 October.
TIC custodial residence does not unambiguously identify beneficial owner or use of proceeds.
U.S. registered funds cannot establish individual emerging-market country destinations.
BEA Q2, WGC September, TIC August and ICI October observations are not contemporaneous.
Institutional editorial review and primary-source spot checks do not constitute an external peer review.
notes: Second editorial review of staged Git blobs after producer revision; the Cloudflare credential failure is operational and separate from QA.

en.title: Global Wealth Flow Monitor — long-term U.S. inflows rebound while short-term positions contract
en.deck: August TIC long-term inflows reversed July's weakness while short-term Treasury and bank liabilities fell; newer fund data reveal selective bond and international-equity demand.
en.regime: Selective long-term securities demand with contracting short-term dollar positions and uneven fund flows.
en.key_risk: A sovereign-yield or concentrated-credit shock could reverse inflows and amplify nonbank liquidity stress.

pt-BR.title: Global Wealth Flow Monitor — recuperação dos fluxos longos para os EUA e contração das posições curtas
pt-BR.deck: O TIC de agosto reverteu a fraqueza de julho em títulos longos, enquanto letras do Tesouro e passivos bancários diminuíram; dados recentes de fundos mostram demanda seletiva por renda fixa e ações internacionais.
pt-BR.regime: Demanda seletiva por títulos longos com redução das posições estrangeiras curtas em dólar e fluxos heterogêneos entre fundos.
pt-BR.key_risk: Choques nos juros soberanos ou no crédito concentrado podem reverter entradas e ampliar tensões de liquidez não bancária.
